name: Dennis Sullivan's house, 134 DeKoven Street

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: Standing on the night of the fire (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 707-715); when it was built is not known, and the scene's phase begins in 1860.

change_note: Built T-3689 (2026-11-20): the O'Leary site on DeKoven Street, on the landmark_1871 archetype in the 1835 town's clapboard and shingles.

placement.position_note: On the 1871 plan's south building line, its front to the street, nearly opposite the O'Leary lot (Andreas vol. 2, p. 708: 'nearly opposite the O'Leary place'). The footprint's origin is local E -310.45 N -1974.85.
placement.symbolic_location: 134 DeKoven Street, south side, nearly opposite the O'Learys.

blocks.name: Sullivan's house
blocks.note: Dennis Sullivan's house at No. 134, 'nearly opposite the O'Leary place' (Andreas vol. 2, p. 708); its size and finish are reconstructed.

fire.note: South of DeKoven Street, against the wind: the fire ran north and east from the barn (Andreas vol. 2, p. 708).

value.note: DENNIS SULLIVAN'S HOUSE, built by T-3689 for the 1871 scene: the house across DeKoven Street from the O'Learys, at No. 134. Sullivan, sitting by the fence in front of it, was the first to see the fire in the barn across the street and ran to it (Andreas vol. 2, p. 708). The fire ran north and east and the houses on the south side of the street stood.

composition.note: Sizes from Andreas's account where he gives them; storeys, roofs and openings from the photograph where it shows them, else reconstructed as the neighbourhood's one-storey frame cottages.

wall_material.value: Painted weatherboards on a frame, a shingle roof

citations.citation: Andreas, A. T. History of Chicago: From the Earliest Period to the Present Time. Vol. 2, From 1857 until the Fire of 1871. Chicago: A. T. Andreas, 1885.
